title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater (Late) on 1970-06-24
source: source: AUD Cassette Master taped by Jim Cooper; Hitachi mics > Hitachi trq-222 deck; Nakamichi Dragon > Benchmark ADC1 24/96 > pc > adobe audition 2.0 > cd wave > flac; transfer & mastering by Rob Berger

ai_review.summary: A clearer‑than‑muddy audience tape captures a tight summer‑1970 performance, with Dark Star and The Other One standing out.
ai_review.review: The recording is an audience (fan) source that many listeners find noticeably clearer and less echo‑laden than other early ’70 tapes, though it retains the expected lo‑fi character. Musically the show is praised as one of the band’s tightest summer performances, with Dark Star and The Other One highlighted as fan‑dream moments and an overall powerful vibe. Most reviewers are enthusiastic, noting the historic aura despite the lack of a soundboard master.

ai_rating.rationale: Multiple detailed reviews (5+) give 4‑5 stars and emphasize strong musical performance plus surprisingly good audio clarity for an audience tape, outweighing the few negative/confusion comments.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clearer than earlier muddy tapes; less echo, decent balance for a fan recording. Still lo‑fi in nature, best enjoyed on modest speakers or “Delco” style playback.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Tight summer ’70 set with acoustic and electric portions; fans note a strong vibe, tight playing, and memorable improvisational sequences.
